edges.effect_quant: A small and mixed literature suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.population: children exposed to antibiotics in the first year of life
edges.mechanism: This early-life or prenatal exposure may shape Inflammatory bowel disease through developmental programming, microbiome establishment, immune maturation, or nutrient sufficiency during sensitive windows. Timing matters because the same exposure can be much more consequential in infancy or pregnancy than later in life.
edges.summary: In children exposed to antibiotics in the first year of life, a small and mixed literature suggest that antibiotic exposure in the first year of life tracks with higher risk of inflammatory bowel disease. Most disagreement in the literature is about size, subgroup sensitivity, or dose threshold rather than about whether the relationship exists at all.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.

evidence.notes: Inflammatory bowel disease and neuropsychiatric disorders: Mechanisms and emerging therapeutics targeting the microbiota-gut-brain axis.
